analysis.title: GS Basics Commodity Disinflation. Technicals. Hynix Multiple. (Rich Privorotsky, 18 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Tech-related markets are recovering off the lows. Nvidia reported a beat and raise with a $130bn guide against roughly $125bn expected, and no China data center compute in the numbers. Privorotsky reads this as spending not stopping.
Nvidia did not hint that Jensen Huang could come back to China, which the market would have liked.
Kospi held the lows of the prior sell-off and was +2%. SK Hynix trades on a 1.79x blended 24-month P/E per Bloomberg.

Tape shift on the prior day: high-beta momentum rose, AI outperformed the AI losers, and the short leg of momentum was hit. Expensive defensives sold off alongside small and mid cap cyclicals. Privorotsky calls this somewhat constructive from a gross positioning standpoint. Korea led a similar pattern in Asia.

Cyber anxiety appears to have hit a local peak. WIRED reports no evidence that the clustered outages were related or caused by hackers. Costco sold out of 21 of 26 high-ticket generator models online by Sunday (Bloomberg), which Privorotsky takes as a read on sentiment.

Trump and Xi are due to meet Thursday in Shenzhen at APEC, with Putin reportedly joining a separate three-way conversation. Privorotsky is watching whether the trade truce holds after the new US chip curbs, and is bearish on a near-term Russia/Ukraine ceasefire. Reports say Ukraine took out the central road span of the Kerch Bridge two days before the meeting.

Oil: the US struck an Iranian missile launch site Tuesday after Iran said it targeted a US radar installation in Bahrain. Oman and Qatar are still talking to Tehran, and Privorotsky sees no clear path to a deal. The US 3-2-1 crack spread fell 36% in six weeks, from $65.56 to $41.90/bbl, and API showed US crude and gasoline stocks each building about 5m barrels.

Metals are weak: London copper is near 5m lows, Shanghai copper is testing 100k, and gold cannot hold a bounce despite lower yields. Privorotsky suggests a liquidation element and that commodities may be signalling policy in China is too tight.

Technicals: CTA selling velocity may have peaked but the remaining magnitude can still be large, especially in Europe. Spot gamma is very level dependent. SPX is holding the 200-day average by a narrow margin, and Nasdaq broke the early-month lows intraday before recovering into the close.

Risk view: Privorotsky is leaning contrarian on AI given the dollars still to be spent, the compression in multiples, and what is being paid for defensives. He sees the broad commodity decline (copper, crude, gasoline, diesel, parts of grains) as a meaningful disinflationary impulse if it persists, and prefers long front-end bonds alongside equities.

Side note: cheap names getting cheaper raises earnings sustainability concerns, but it is hard to press lower. If the view is bearish on AI/growth, he suggests expressing it in other pockets given the margin of safety in names like SK Hynix.
